objective: Serialize mounted note saves without losing the newest value when it returns to an earlier saved text.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Current React async effects and derived rendering.

relevanceRationale.transferable: Transfers to caching,identity,concurrency and state consistency.

defects: All authored styles can lose a return-to-previously-saved value while another payload is in flight.
The brief conflates mounted serialization and immediate unmount flush; clarify the bounded contract.
rationale: All three styles skipped the debounce when the newest text equalled the old saved value,even while a different value was being written. A four-positive-program native diagnostic isolates the missed follow-up write; busy-aware guards repair it. The prompt and skeleton clarify the in-flight exception,the successful-queue rule and mounted serialization; failed writes offer Retry for the newest text. Empty strings,multiline bodies,non-ok failures and repeated Retry during a pending write are exercised. The existing missing-saved-ref QA remains negative. Unmount flushing is best effort and may overlap a pending write; this exercise does not prove browser-unload delivery or backend write ordering,reflected in explanation3/5.

defects: Junior/senior examples omit the requested scaling plan and globally lose comments.
Original groups never exceed four posts and never select the same author twice.
rationale: A fifteen-post model exposes a nine-post author bucket,checks numeric author order and every arrival-ordered title,then repeats and switches selections while exactly one aria-pressed stays true and no new request occurs. Empty success keeps no authors/posts/error. Both alternative published styles already use reduce correctly; they need the requested scaling comments rather than an algorithm rewrite.
